scientific_card_excerpt.text: Claim: Define LY(r), r>1, by zero-freeness of the flattened polynomial f_K(z,w)=sum_xy K_xy z^x w^y when all variables lie in the open polydisk of radius r. For every complex 2^n-by-2^n K in LY(r), the maximum-modulus eigenvalue is unique, nonzero and algebraically simple, and every other eigenvalue obeys |lambda/lambda_*|<=r^-2; its rank-one spectral projector factors into LY(r) vectors. Also, if K_1,...,K_T each lie in LY(r), M=K_T...K_1, e=|0^n>, and a=e^T M e !=0, then B=(Me)(e^T M)/a has rank one and ||M-B||_F <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||Me||_2 <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||M||_2.

COMPLEX LEE–YANG TRANSFER: SPECTRAL SEPARATION AND FINITE-PRODUCT COLLAPSE
10 October 2026. Internally reconstructed scoped result; novelty unestablished.
This does NOT pass the foundational-discovery gate.

Provenance and imports
----------------------
The PSD spectral-ratio theorem and its squeezing/Schwarz mechanism are due to
Bravyi, Gosset, Liu and Wong, arXiv:2607.14401v1 (15 July 2026):
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.14401v1
Their quantum ground-energy algorithm is prior work, not our discovery.
We extend the stated PSD theorem to complex matrices, and give a quantitative
finite-product norm consequence. The central squeezing mechanism is imported
and adapted, not claimed as a new general principle. Complex projective
contraction has older antecedents, including Rugh (2010),
https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2010.171.1707 .

For a tensor v with n binary indices set f_v(z)=sum_x v_x z^x. Write LY(r)
if f_v has no zeros when every |z_i|<r. A matrix K on n qubits is flattened
with f_K(z,w)=sum_xy K_xy z^x w^y. No conjugation is used in contractions.
Here D_a denotes the open n-dimensional polydisk of radius a.

We import two standard facts, stated precisely as Facts 1–2 in the source:
(i) contracting two binary tensor indices preserves zero-freeness in the
remaining radii when the product of the contracted radii exceeds 1;
(ii) a nonzero coefficientwise limit of tensors in LY(r) is in LY(r).
Tensor products and nonzero scalar multiples preserve LY. Thus K in LY(r)
maps any vector in LY(s) to a NONZERO vector in LY(r) if rs>1. Products of
matrices in LY(r), r>1, remain in LY(r); their (0,0) entries are nonzero.
These facts include cancellation control; positivity is not being assumed.

THEOREM A — arbitrary complex spectrum
---------------------------------------
Let n>=1, r>1, and let K be ANY complex 2^n by 2^n matrix in LY(r).
It has a unique eigenvalue lambda_* of largest modulus, that eigenvalue is
nonzero and algebraically simple, and every other eigenvalue satisfies

                  |lambda/lambda_*| <= r^(-2).

Both factors of its rank-one spectral projector are LY(r), with the left
factor interpreted as a bilinear covector. No PSD, normality, diagonalizability,
or sign condition on K is needed. The ratio is sharp already for n=1:
diag(1,r^(-2)) has polynomial 1+r^(-2)zw and lies in LY(r).

Proof, conditional comparison. Suppose first K psi=lambda_* p

ERRATA AND EVIDENCE PRECEDENCE — 2026-10-10

All investigator reports are preliminary research records. A FAIL or
UNRESOLVED verdict is not an endorsement of every intermediate calculation.
The following errors were found; this is not a claim that no others remain.

Precedence: the five retained scoped derivations and this errata index,
then the explicit dated errata and focused audits, then the preliminary
reports. Later errata take precedence over earlier conflicting arithmetic.
Only claims explicitly discussed in a focused audit were audited. Do not
treat a filename containing 'freeze' or a report's self-description as a
cryptographic commitment; version-complete immutable snapshots were not made.

round1/01.txt: A scan-based simulation does not itself prove the invoked
O(t log t) universal-simulation overhead. That overhead must be imported from
an appropriate efficient universal-simulation theorem. No new hierarchy
theorem or self-contained proof of that simulation result was established.

round1/03.txt: For u=a cos(N x_1)(e_2+e_3) on a periodic domain containing
whole periods, ||u||_2^2=a^2 Vol and ||curl u||_2^2=a^2 N^2 Vol. The report's
values were twice these. Energy control is supercritical for the regularity
problem; the terminology 'subcritical' in that discussion must be corrected.

round1/12.txt: A width-w bucket has at most 2*3^w clauses containing either
polarity of the eliminated variable, not 3^w. The larger displayed headline
9^(w+1) bound still accommodates this count. See round1/12_challenge.txt.
The method is standard Davis–Putnam elimination with a supplied width bound.

round1/23_challenge.txt: For pure amplitudes (1,1,i)/sqrt(3), the matrix entry
rho_12 is -i/3, not +i/3 (zero-based labels). Reverse the corresponding block
phase. The phase-alignment principle and adjacent-coherence formula survive.

round1/24.txt: If two rounds each measure points with error at most rho,
true old positions have minimum separation Delta, and displacement is at
most eta, the sufficient nearest-neighbour margin is
2 eta + 4 rho < Delta. The weaker reported 2 eta + 2 rho margin is inadequate
under that measurement model.

round2/05.txt: The flat-profile overlap 1-n/(2L) is valid only for n<=L;
the general expression is E[(1-W/L)_+] for W~Bin(n,1/2). The uniform sine
